record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; referenced code and other files were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports a weight-edited release and outcomes for refusal and coding capability. This tests practical removal with a different method from activation projection.
record.gate_note: The README reports refusal and coding-capability outcomes for the edited model. Performance benchmarks and the reported KL are not rows because they do not directly measure the claim versions. The listed recipe/configuration files were not read or run.
record.test_reason: A self-reported model release that applies a weight-edit abliteration (norm-preserving biprojection, expert-granular, router suppression) to a hybrid MoE/SSM thinking model. It reports refusal counts and a coding probe against the base, so it bears on V2 (practical removal in a released model) using a variant method.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The README claims refusals were removed (0/80) with no coding-capability loss (pass@1 0.833, same as base) and near-lossless KL. It also claims the NVFP4 quantization matches BF16.
record.recipe_differences: This is a model-release repository, not a replication. The README describes abliterix weight edits, including expert-granular edits and router suppression, rather than reporting the original activation projection at every layer and position or adding the direction.
record.method_sensitivity: The README says the lowest-refusal trial was over-abliterated and produced word salad, while a much lighter expert edit was selected as coherent with the same reported refusal removal.
record.problems: Results are self-reported in the README. The harmful-prompt evaluation is 80 prompts, the coding probe is 18 tasks, and no uncertainty estimates or evaluation protocol details are given. The reported base refusal figure is approximately 94/100 and is not the same-sized prompt set. Repository code was not read or run.
record.rows_left_out: None of the README's refusal or coding-capability results were omitted. Performance benchmarks and KL were left out because they do not directly report the refusal or capability behavior specified by the tested version.

untested.parts: Only one model is tested. Capability is checked only by an 18-task coding probe and first-token KL; there are no broad benchmarks on the edited model. Terminal-Bench and SWE-bench figures are base-model context, not measured after the edit.
No difference-in-means direction analysis, no addition/induction test, no activation-level ablation.
The model is a thinking model, but whether a single direction mediates refusal in reasoning models is not examined.

missing.what: The lowest-refusal Optuna trial was over-abliterated and gave word-salad generations; the shipped edit is 170× lighter with the same refusal removal. No numbers are given.
missing.locator: README, How it was built, stage 3

missing.what: A pre-abliteration SSM conv1d outlier repair (layers 36/37) was required to prevent coherence collapse.
missing.locator: README, How it was built, stage 1

missing.what: First-token KL vs base of about 0.0014, a capability-preservation indicator.

record.verdict_notes: This is a self-reported, non-peer-reviewed model card. The refusal judge, prompt sources and decoding settings for the evaluation are not given, and the base baseline was measured on a different prompt set. The method credits Arditi et al. but uses grimjim norm-preserving biprojection plus expert-granular edits and router suppression, so it is a variant of directional ablation. The KL, the over-abliteration failure and the SSM repair are not recorded as rows; they should be added so the limits_scope verdict has row support.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means direction is tested by projection at every layer and position, and no addition/steering test is reported.
Only one released model is reported. Capability preservation is assessed with an 18-task agentic-coding probe, not a broad set of abilities.
No attack that suppresses the direction or training against its ablation is tested.
The README does not compare a single direction with an affine set, cone, or multiple directions.
No harmfulness judgment is measured separately from refusal.
No transfer across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct stages is tested.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or timing is reported.
The README calls the model a thinking model but does not test whether V1 holds for reasoning models.

tranche.reason: It reports refusal removal and capability retention from a weight-edit abliteration, but with a modified method: norm-preserving biprojection, expert-granular edits, router suppression and an Optuna search. That is a different method aimed at V2. T3 (new hybrid MoE/SSM setting) is also defensible.

source_check.notes: The text is the README only; RECIPE.md, config and AGENTS.md contents are absent. No row records the first-token KL (~0.0014 vs base) or the over-abliterated trial's word salad. The repo description says 'BF16 + FP8', but the README says FP8 is not viable and NVFP4 shipped. It is a thinking model, but nothing measures V8 directly.

statements.correction: Ornith-1.0-35B: hybrid qwen3_5_moe, 40 layers (30 GatedDeltaNet + 10 full-attn), 256 experts + shared. SSM conv1d outlier blocks (layers 36/37) rescaled before abliteration. GatedDeltaNet/SSM internals and vision tower not modified by the edit.
statements.problem: Accurate for this study: Ornith-1.0-35B is a hybrid, not a pure SSM. The statement credits the conv1d rescaling only to gh:aeon-7/qwen3.6-27b, but this study also did it. Also, this edit left the SSM layers untouched.
